scope.selection: Purposive first collection of reusable scientific ontologies and thesauri, chosen for cross-disciplinary coverage and inspectable licensing. Not an exhaustive search or a random sample.

method.unit: One normalized text string with two or more distinct IRIs, counted once across the captured collections.
method.normalization: Unicode NFKC, lowercase, whitespace collapse and trim.
method.included: All supplied labels and synonyms, identifier fallback labels, all supplied languages, and obsolete terms. Repeated use of one IRI across sources counts as one identifier.
notEstablished: That each different IRI represents a different meaning.
That each candidate is a scientific error or contradiction.
That imported assertions are empirically true.
That every scientific entity, law, operation, unit or source has been collected.
That a matching dimension or label permits physical transfer.

review.status: Candidates awaiting semantic review. Zero here means none established by this audit, not that none exist.

coverageGaps: No completeness criterion defining every scientific concept or operation.
Uneven depth: biomedical sources dominate this first capture.
Scientific claims, equations, experimental observations and executable contracts require separate admission.
Source ontology versions, provenance, language tagging, aliases and deprecated terms need ongoing review.
Some external targets and complex OWL expressions remain outside the browser projection.

certification.claim: Reproducible audit receipt for this captured dataset.
certification.not: Third-party certification, a signed authenticity certificate, a proof of scientific truth or a completeness certificate.
nextGates: Review candidate pairs for shared identity, different meanings, language differences, historical replacements and actual contradictions.
Define scope and coverage targets for each scientific field.
Validate reviewed mappings against source axioms and negative transfer tests.
Seek independent domain review and publish disagreements and corrections.
